headline: Tanker strikes put Brent at $111 into a 5.15% ten-year, and Korea's AI complex broke another 3.7% overnight — yesterday's two sources of relief both reversed in one session.
summary: The oil relief lasted exactly one day, and this time the shock is seaborne. Brent +1.6% to 111.34, +7.2% on the month and at the 88th percentile of its year, while WTI went the other way, -3.0% to 100.60 — a Brent-WTI dislocation consistent with strikes on tankers in the Gulf rather than a demand impulse. Oil/gold is +7.8% on the week and sits at the 95th percentile, +83.7% YTD; DBC is at the 99.5th percentile of its 52-week range. The inflation composite is -28. The offsets are real but second-order: RBOB -2.0% today and -11.3% on the month (z=-1.15), corn -11.2%, wheat -7.4%, and 10-year breakevens unchanged on the day at 2.35%, up only 2bp in a month. The bond market is not pricing a new inflation regime yet. It is pricing a higher real clearing rate.

Rates remain the binding constraint and the worst composite on the board at -58, unchanged from yesterday. 10y 5.15% (+6bp, +14bp on the month), 30y 5.48%, 5y 4.94%, and the 10-year real yield 2.80% — 28.4% above its 200-day and +87bp YTD. MOVE 101.3, +25.6% in a month. 2s10s steepened another 3bp to 38bp with acceleration z=1.45: the long end is leading, which is the wrong kind of steepening. The clearing price nobody has answered is the 30-year mortgage at 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, 100th percentile of the year. Housing confirms it: ITB and XHB sit at the 5.4th and 4.7th percentiles, XHB/SPY at the 3.8th, DHI -2.9%. A supply-driven crude shock landing on a 2.80% real yield is the single most dangerous combination on this tape.

The narrow US squeeze did not survive the overnight. Monday's bid was five tickers — NDX +1.2%, SOXX +1.7%, AMZN +5.0%, PLTR +4.4%, TSLA +3.8% — against RSP/SPY -0.7% and XLF -0.8%. Today KOSPI -3.7% to 5,552.7, now -19.5% on the month with z=-2.75 and acceleration z=-2.54, the two worst readings anywhere in the digest; Monday's +4.1% pop in EWY is already gone. Taiwan -1.1%, Nikkei -1.3%, Hang Seng -1.3%, Shanghai -4.5% on the month, Euro Stoxx -0.9%, CAC -0.8% and at the 13th percentile. Semis are the transmission line: SMH -4.3% on the month with 1m relative strength -4.9%, SOXX -5.8%, MU -10.9%, AVGO -6.3%. The AI-power derivatives keep dying outright — REMX -22.7% on the month and 37.3% below its 200-day at the 0th percentile, NLR -13.4% (0th), URA -15.3% (0th), GRID -5.1%. And the hedges that came off Monday are being repriced: VIX +1.5% to 18.71, +22.5% on the week, turning up with z=1.01; VIX/VIX3M at 0.941 with z=1.80; SKEW 161.86 at the 84th percentile. Vol is still only at the 30th percentile of its year — that is the cheap part of this.

Two things genuinely improved and one new fracture opened. Credit stopped deteriorating: leveraged loans recovered from z=-1.36 to z=-0.86, HYG/IEF +0.3% on the day, HYG flat — still weak (z=-1.14, 28.8th percentile) but no longer making the day's new low. Asian funding is calm despite the equity carnage: USDKRW -0.4% to 1,327.5 at the 0th percentile of its range, USDCNY -0.4% also at the 0th, CEW +0.1% — this is a positioning unwind, not a dollar squeeze. The new fracture is Mexico. USDMXN +7.6% in a month at z=2.81 with acceleration z=1.69 — the largest z-score on the entire tape — while MXX equity is +8.9% on the month (z=1.91) and EWW only +2.8%. The peso is paying for the index. Brazil is the clean side of LatAm: USDBRL -1.5% on the month and rolling over, EWZ +11.8% with relative strength +11.1% vs SPX. Elsewhere leadership is unchanged and defensive-plus-energy: XLE 98.3rd percentile, XOP 98.8th, XOM 99th, CVX 99.2nd, XLV +4.7% on the month with acceleration z=1.60, XLP acc z=1.89, WMT and COST both +11.2%. Risk regime -19, flat on the day — but the composition shifted again, from a credit crack to a commodity shock plus an Asian growth crack. Liquidity offers no cushion: RRP is effectively zero at $0.33bn while the TGA rebuilt +8.7% on the week to $948bn.

good.text: The pump is deflating even as crude spikes: RBOB -2.0% today, -11.3% on the month at z=-1.15, corn -11.2%, wheat -7.4%. 10y breakevens unchanged at 2.35% and only +2bp in a month, 5y at 2.38% and rolling over. The oil move is not yet in the inflation expectation.

Credit stopped making new lows. BKLN z improved from -1.36 to -0.86, HYG/IEF +0.3% on the day, HYG unchanged at 76.83. Still the weak link (HYG at the 28.8th percentile), but the one-day divergence that defined yesterday has closed.

No Asian funding stress underneath the Asian equity crash: USDKRW -0.4% to 1,327.5 at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, USDCNY -0.4% also 0th, CEW +0.1% and still up 4.3% YTD. This reads as de-grossing, not dollar shortage.

Energy equity owns the top of the range and today it has the commodity behind it: XLE at the 98.3rd percentile with 1m relative strength +5.4%, XOP 98.8th (+4.4% rs), XOM 99th, CVX 99.2nd. Brent +7.2% on the month validates the leadership rather than contradicting it.

The cyclical metal is holding while the monetary metals liquidate: copper +0.5% at the 87.7th percentile, copper/gold +1.0% and at the 95.7th percentile with z=0.88. Growth pulse composite +8 — demand is not what is breaking.

Brazil remains the only clean relative-strength trade outside energy and healthcare: EWZ +11.8% on the month with rs +11.1% vs SPX, BVSP z=1.80 at the 93.9th percentile, USDBRL -1.5% on the month and rolling over.

bad.text: A supply-side oil shock: Brent +1.6% to 111.34 and +7.2% on the month while WTI fell 3.0% to 100.60 — seaborne risk premium, not demand. Oil/gold at the 95th percentile and +83.7% YTD, DBC at the 99.5th. This is a tax on every margin outside energy.

The long end keeps repricing higher: 10y 5.15% (+14bp/1m), 30y 5.48%, 10y real yield 2.80% and 28.4% above its 200-day. MOVE 101.3, +25.6% in a month. 2s10s steepening with acceleration z=1.45 led by the 30y — term premium, not easing.

Housing is the unhealed wound: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +64bp on the month, z=1.91, 100th percentile. ITB -1.7% and XHB at the 4.7th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 3.8th and 15.8% below its 200-day, DHI -2.9%. Nothing in the equity tape has touched it.

Korea's AI unwind is accelerating, not bottoming: KOSPI -3.7% to 5,552.7, -19.5% on the month, z=-2.75 with acceleration z=-2.54 — the worst pair of readings on the tape. SMH -4.3%/1m with rs -4.9%, MU -10.9%, AVGO -6.3%. The AI-capex derivatives are at 0th percentiles: REMX -22.7%, NLR -13.4%, URA -15.3%.

Hedges are being bought back one day after being dumped: VIX +1.5% to 18.71 and +22.5% on the week (z=1.01, turning up), VIX/VIX3M 0.941 with z=1.80, SKEW 161.86 at the 84th percentile. Global cash markets confirm — Euro Stoxx -0.9%, Nikkei -1.3%, Hang Seng -1.3%.

Under the index, appetite is still contracting: Russell 2000 -4.6% on the month, IWM/SPY at the 6.6th percentile, KRE -4.3% with rs -11.4% over 3m, JETS -9.4%, IAI -6.1%, high-beta/low-vol -8.0% on the week. And the TGA rebuilt +8.7% to $948bn with RRP at $0.33bn — no liquidity buffer left to absorb it.

trades.name: Short long-duration Treasuries (TLT)
trades.line: Short TLT: $111 Brent into a 5.15% 10y and a 7.40% mortgage
trades.expr: Buy TLT Dec 78/72 put spread, or short ZB futures 1x. Alternative cash expression: short TLT, long IEF 1.5x notional to isolate the 10s30s bear-steepener.
trades.thesis: A seaborne crude supply shock is landing on a bond market whose real yield is already 2.80% and 28.4% above its 200-day. Term premium, not inflation expectation, is doing the work — 2s10s steepened 3bp with acceleration z=1.45 while 10y breakevens were unchanged at 2.35%. That combination keeps pressure on the 30y.
trades.trigger: Brent +1.6% to 111.34 and +7.2% on the month; 10y +6bp to 5.15% and +14bp on the month; 30y 5.48%; MOVE 101.3 and +25.6% in a month; the 30-year mortgage at 7.40%, z=1.91, 100th percentile.
trades.stop: TLT back above 82 (roughly +3.2% from 79.46), or the 10y closing below 5.00% with Brent back under $100.

trades.name: Long XOP / short JETS
trades.line: Long XOP / short JETS: fuel cost squeeze on the fuel burners
trades.expr: Long XOP, short JETS, dollar-neutral. Size at 1.0x each leg; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: Brent at 111 is revenue for E&P and a direct cost line for airlines and freight. The relative strength is already in motion and the oil move is supply-driven, so it will not be demand-rescued.
trades.trigger: Brent +7.2% on the month to 111.34 (88th percentile) with XOP at the 98.8th percentile and 1m rs +4.4%; JETS -1.0% today, -9.4% on the month, z=-1.11, 1m rs -9.9%; IYT 3m rs -12.9%, XTN -16.2% over 3m.
trades.stop: Brent sustained back below $100 (WTI already there at 100.60), or the pair giving back 6% from entry.

trades.name: Short Korea (EWY)
trades.line: Short EWY: Korea's AI unwind is accelerating, not bottoming
trades.expr: Short EWY outright, or buy Dec EWY puts ~10% OTM. Fade into any 3-5% bounce; keep size modest given the -19.5% month already behind us.
trades.thesis: The memory/AI-capex trade is unwinding at a pace with no precedent on this tape, and Monday's +4.1% EWY pop was a positioning bounce that lasted one session. With KOSPI still only at the 32.8th percentile of its 52-week range after a 19.5% monthly fall, there is room below.
trades.trigger: KOSPI -3.7% today to 5,552.7, z=-2.75 and acceleration z=-2.54 — the worst readings in the digest — 14.7% below its 200-day; SMH -4.3% on the month with rs -4.9%, MU -10.9%, SOXX -7.9% on the week.
trades.stop: EWY recovering above ~170 (+8% from 156.58) or KOSPI reclaiming its 200-day; also exit if USDKRW turns up sharply from 1,327.5, which would change this from de-grossing into something policymakers must defend.

trades.name: Long EWZ / short EWW
trades.line: Long EWZ / short EWW: BRL firm, MXN cracking at z=2.81
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, equal dollars. Both are USD-denominated, so the pair is effectively long BRL-assets vs short MXN-assets.
trades.thesis: USD/MXN is the single most extreme move on the board and the Mexican equity index is masking it in local terms — the FX is eating the return for dollar investors. Brazil has the opposite mix: a firming currency and an index at the 94th percentile.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +7.6% on the month, z=2.81 with acceleration z=1.69, 5.8% above its 200-day; MXX +8.9% on the month but EWW only +2.8%; versus USDBRL -1.5% on the month and rolling over, EWZ +11.8% with 1m rs +11.1% vs SPX and BVSP z=1.80.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 17.7 (-4%) with acceleration turning negative, or a 6% drawdown in the pair.

trades.name: Long volatility into a cheap curve
trades.line: Buy VIX Nov calls: 18.7 with the whole global tape down
trades.expr: VIX Nov 22/30 call spread, or an SPX Dec 5% OTM / 10% OTM put spread. Prefer the index put spread if you want carry-light downside rather than a vol-of-vol bet.
trades.thesis: Spot vol is turning up from only the 30th percentile of its year while the term structure is still upward-sloping and SKEW is at the 84th percentile — tail demand is high, near-dated vol is not. An oil supply shock plus an accelerating Asian equity unwind is exactly the setup that inverts the curve.
trades.trigger: VIX +1.5% to 18.71 and +22.5% on the week, turning up with z=1.01; VIX/VIX3M 0.941 with z=1.80 and acceleration z=1.02; SKEW 161.86; Euro Stoxx -0.9%, Nikkei -1.3%, Hang Seng -1.3%, KOSPI -3.7% overnight.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.90 with SPX printing a new high above 7,690.7.
trades.target: VIX 26 and the term structure inverted above 1.00.

trades.name: Long XLV / short XLI
trades.line: Long XLV / short XLI: cost shock hits machines, not pharma
trades.expr: Long XLV, short XLI, dollar-neutral. Can be sharpened with LLY/UNH on the long leg against CAT/ETN on the short.
trades.thesis: Healthcare is the only sector with improving relative strength and positive acceleration; industrials are rolling over into a rising energy and freight cost base with a 5.15% 10y on top. Defensive leadership has now hardened for three straight sessions.
trades.trigger: XLV +4.7% on the month, 1m rs +4.1% and turning up, acceleration z=1.60, 95.7th percentile; XLI -1.5% on the month, rolling over, 3m rs -9.4%, 3.3% below its 200-day; CAT -10.3% on the month (z=-1.41), ETN -7.8% (z=-1.32), GEV -3.4%.
trades.stop: XLV 1m relative strength turning negative, or XLI reclaiming its 200-day and holding.

trades.name: Short home construction (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.40% mortgage, 100th percentile, no relief
trades.expr: Buy ITB Jan puts ~8% OTM, or short ITB against a long in XLV to stay sector-neutral on beta.
trades.thesis: The mortgage rate is at the highest level in its entire 52-week range and rising 64bp a month while the 10y pushes 5.15%. Homebuilder equities have bounced on nothing but a weak-dollar hope; the financing cost has not improved a single basis point.
trades.trigger: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +64bp on the month, z=1.91, 100th percentile, 14.4% above its 200-day; ITB -1.7% on a day the S&P rose 0.4%; XHB/SPY at the 3.8th percentile and 15.8% below its 200-day; DHI -2.9%.
trades.stop: The 30-year mortgage breaking back below 7.00%, or ITB closing above its 200-day (currently 11.3% above spot).
